paragraphs: Sheffield City Council runs its own fostering service, and children from the city also live with independent agencies such as the services shown above. Ofsted inspected the council's children's services in September 2023 and rated them good overall, with the experiences and progress of children in care judged outstanding.

The council's placement sufficiency strategy for 2023 to 2026 counted 634 children looked after on 31 July 2023. Just over half lived in the council's own provision, a higher share than in similar areas or England as a whole. The strategy found that 37% of children were placed outside the city, although three in four lived within 20 miles of home, and one of its aims is to provide local homes in Sheffield so that young people can keep in touch with the people who matter to them. It sets out to strengthen foster carer capacity that meets Sheffield children's needs, notes that 14% of children in care have a disability, with a commitment to overnight respite for disabled children, and plans more supported lodgings for young people as the number of unaccompanied children seeking asylum has grown.

To foster with the council you need to be at least 21, live in the UK full time and have at least one spare bedroom; there is no upper age limit and some people foster into their seventies. No qualifications are needed. You can be single if you have a network of support, rent your home if it is stable, work, receive benefits, have a disability, keep pets or be LGBTQ+. Smokers can foster, though not children under five or children with health conditions or disabilities. You do not need to drive, but you must be able to get children to school, and past convictions that do not relate to children may not rule you out.

Council carers start with three days of pre-approval training, then induction courses in the first year. They have their own supervising social worker, a mentor when they are new, monthly support groups, a 24-hour support line, breaks between placements, and access to the fostering service's psychologist and speech and language therapist. You can ask for an information pack or join an online information evening.

An agency approves and supports its carers itself and looks after children for councils including Sheffield. Compare the council with two or three of the services above, and ask each about pay, training and support. If you live outside the city, see our pages for Rotherham, Barnsley, Doncaster, Derbyshire and South Yorkshire.
